commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: National association representing DMEPOS suppliers, manufacturers, and other homecare stakeholders supplying oxygen, PAP, ventilators, complex rehabilitation technology, urological, ostomy, wound care, and other home medical equipment and services.

executive_summary: AAHomecare supports ePA modernization but focuses on DMEPOS prior authorization burdens, patient access delays, rural supplier impacts, and the gap between FHIR-based automation and DME supplier technology capacity. It requests retroactive authorization protections for urgent equipment delivery, MA plan FFS-parity enforcement, gold carding, standardized documentation checklists, supplier technology support, renewal/status data in PA APIs, structured CRT documentation standards, granular denial metrics, and AI guardrails.

regulatory_citations_mentioned: CY 2024 MA and Part D Final Rule
Medicare FFS coverage and documentation requirements
standards_referenced: AI / natural language processing for PA-relevant clinical findings

detailed_positions.topic: DMEPOS PA delays and patient harm
detailed_positions.rationale: DMEPOS PA approvals commonly take one to four weeks, delaying hospital discharge, respiratory therapy, mobility equipment, and activities of daily living, especially for rural and underserved beneficiaries.
detailed_positions.specific_request: CMS should reform DMEPOS PA processes to reduce delays, administrative burden, supplier attrition, and access barriers.

detailed_positions.topic: Retroactive authorization for urgent DME delivery
detailed_positions.rationale: Urgent clinical circumstances may require equipment delivery before PA completion, and process-based denials after delivery discourage suppliers from meeting urgent needs.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Create a retroactive authorization pathway, e.g., submission within 72 hours after urgent delivery, prohibit denials solely for post-delivery timing with urgency attestation, and require granular denial reason reporting to distinguish procedural from clinical denials.

detailed_positions.topic: MA plan DMEPOS FFS parity and criteria transparency
detailed_positions.rationale: MA plan DMEPOS PA criteria can exceed or narrow Medicare FFS LCD and Policy Article requirements, and decisions may be inconsistent with published criteria.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Require annual CMS review of MA DMEPOS PA criteria, create a beneficiary/supplier complaint process, publish machine-readable MAC LCD/Policy Article criteria, require standardized public criteria updates, and require denial reasons identifying the specific criterion not met.

detailed_positions.rationale: Repeated PA for high-performing suppliers, prescribers, stable patients, replacements, repairs, and routine supplies creates burden with limited program integrity value.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Finalize strong DMEPOS gold carding with transparent thresholds and automatic qualification; create streamlined renewal pathways and a 90-day continuity-of-authorization standard when beneficiaries change plans.

detailed_positions.rationale: Many DMEPOS suppliers lack native EMR integration or capacity to build direct FHIR API integrations, especially small and rural suppliers.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Provide a no-cost CMS-facilitated shared-service PA portal, technical assistance grants, and ensure mandates do not impose additional payer/subcontractor overhead costs on providers.

detailed_positions.topic: PA API renewal and status information
detailed_positions.rationale: DMEPOS suppliers need proactive authorization management to avoid lapses in oxygen, ventilators, power wheelchairs, enteral nutrition, and other long-term equipment.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Require payer PA APIs to include authorization expiration date and renewal eligibility data in all PA determination responses.

detailed_positions.rationale: CRT documentation may span 20 to 40 pages and current ePA systems cannot reliably process unstructured functional assessments.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Invest in structured, computable data standards for CRT functional assessments that support automated review while preserving individualized clinical evaluation.

detailed_positions.rationale: AI tools could improve consistency but may also apply vague or overly restrictive criteria, deny based on population-level data, or prioritize cost reduction over individualized review.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Require qualified human review before AI-assisted denials, prohibit AI criteria more restrictive than CMS-published LCD standards, and mandate disclosure when AI influenced a PA determination.

solicitation_responses.summary: Requests granular denial reason reporting, including differentiation of procedural versus clinical denials and identification of the specific LCD or Policy Article criterion not met.
Addresses urgent DME circumstances where standard timelines are clinically impractical and requests retroactive authorization protections.
Requests DMEPOS PA approval, denial, appeal overturn, and product-category reporting to support CMS oversight and supplier benchmarking.

solicitation_responses.solicitation: RFI: Prior authorization and laboratory/testing timing analog
solicitation_responses.summary: Analogizes specimen-collection timing denials to urgent DME delivery before PA completion and requests retroactive authorization safeguards.
Requests shared-service PA portal, technical assistance, machine-readable criteria, renewal data, structured CRT documentation standards, and AI safeguards.

key_quotes: Prior authorization requirements often delay access to essential equipment.
Technology can improve submission efficiency, but it cannot fix PA criteria that are unpublished, ambiguous, or more restrictive than FFS requirements.
The majority of DMEPOS suppliers operate with supplier management software and billing systems that are not natively integrated with hospital system EMR platforms.
agency_action_requested: Use the rulemaking/RFIs to reform DMEPOS PA by enforcing FFS parity, reducing renewals, protecting urgent deliveries, supporting small supplier ePA access, improving documentation standards, publishing machine-readable criteria, and regulating AI use.
